extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, IP law firms, legal analytics users, in-house counsel
extracted.subtask_description: A press-release summary of Lex Machina's 2024 Patent Litigation Report describing the metrics, trends, and datasets the report uses to analyze patent litigation across district courts, federal appellate courts, and the PTAB (covering 2021–2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent case filings (annual counts and trend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of patent cases filed per year (e.g., 'In 2023, 3,111 patent cases were filed, continuing the steady decline of patent case filings since 2021').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to track overall activity in patent litigation and identify multi-year trends; report notes the decrease is likely linked to drops in filings by high-volume plaintiffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-volume plaintiff filings (contribution to trends)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and trends of cases filed by high-volume plaintiffs (the report indicates the drop in overall filings is likely driven, at least in part, by fewer cases from high-volume plaintiffs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter/segment data to isolate high-volume plaintiff activity to understand its impact on aggregate filing trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue activity (district-level case share)
rubrics_metrics.description: District court activity measured by share and counts of patent cases filed in each district (e.g., 'The Western District of Texas was the most active district from 2021 to 2023 with 22% of all patent cases filed', but filings in that court dropped in 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare district shares and year-over-year changes to identify active venues and shifts caused by external factors (e.g., judicial orders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge assignment volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of patent cases assigned to individual judges (e.g., 'Judge Albright was assigned to the highest number of patent cases from 2021 to 2023 with 1,844 cases', with noted declines in 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use judge-level assignment counts to identify judges with heavy patent dockets and to spot changes in assignment patterns over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law firm activity by side (representation counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of cases in which particular law firms represented plaintiffs or defendants (e.g., 'Ramey represented plaintiffs in the highest number of patent cases ... Fish & Richardson represented defendants in the highest number of cases').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track firm-level activity to identify high-volume plaintiff and defense counsel, competitive positioning, and potential referral/engagement opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal appellate reversal rate (patent cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of patent cases appealed to federal appellate courts that were ultimately reversed on the merits (e.g., 'For patent cases that were appealed ... 34% were ultimately reversed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appellate reversal rates to assess the risk/likelihood of reversal on appeal and inform appellate strategy and settlement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages awarded — totals and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate damages awarded statistics, including totals and counts for specific damages types (e.g., '$6 billion in total damages were awarded as Reasonable Royalty across 129 cases' from 2021–2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze damages totals and distributions (by damages type, industry, or case subset) to inform valuation expectations and settlement benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB petitions filed (counts and trends)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of petitions filed at the Patent Trial and Appeal Board and year-over-year movement (e.g., 'The number of PTAB petitions filed dropped in 2023').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track filing volume to gauge PTAB activity levels and to spot shifts in petitioning behavior by challengers or industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB institution rate (percent of petitions instituted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share/percentage of PTAB petitions that resulted in instituted trials (e.g., 'slight increase in instituted trials ... from 51% to 54%').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institution rates to assess probability a petition will lead to trial, which affects cost-benefit analyses for filing or defending petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB appellate reversal rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of PTAB cases appealed to federal appellate courts that were ultimately reversed on the merits (e.g., 'For PTAB cases that were appealed ... 22% were ultimately reversed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ PTAB appeal reversal statistics to evaluate appellate risk and to compare PTAB outcomes with district-court appeal behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most active PTAB petitioners (identity and counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of top petitioning entities by volume (e.g., 'Samsung was the most active petitioner in PTAB petitions filed during the three-year period').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify repeat petitioners to analyze strategies, target industries, or potential adversaries/partners at the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law firm activity in PTAB (representation counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of PTAB petitions handled by law firms (e.g., 'Fish & Richardson represented parties in the highest number of petitions filed from 2021 to 2023').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track PTAB counsel activity to find experienced PTAB practitioners and benchmark firm market share in inter partes review practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing metrics (case timing and duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures related to timing in litigation and PTAB practice (report scope includes 'timing metrics' though specific timing statistics are contained in the full report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use timing metrics (e.g., time to decision, time to trial/institution) to plan case schedules, manage client expectations, and evaluate forum speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case resolutions and findings (outcome classifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of how cases terminate (resolutions) and substantive findings reported in cases (the report surveys 'case resolutions, findings, and damages').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment outcomes (dismissal, settlement, judgment, findings of infringement/invalidity) to assess success rates and guide procedural and substantive strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset filtering / case segmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to filter cases to provide analytics on different subsets, such as general patent, high-volume plaintiff, ANDA, PTAB, and federal appellate cases (the report 'often focuses on different sets of data, e.g., filtering cases ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use filters to generate targeted analytics for specific practice questions (e.g., ANDA litigation trends vs. general patent litigation) and to produce more actionable, context-specific insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of analytics for litigation strategy decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how the report's metrics can be used: 'The metrics in this report can help readers decide who to pursue as clients, whether to file a particular motion, or when to settle (and for how much).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the report's data-driven insights to client development, motion practice, and settlement strategy — leveraging observed trends (venue, judge, firm, damages, institution rates) to inform decisions.
